newsitem.title: USA: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady Monday-dealers.
newsitem.headline: US Midwest direct hogs seen steady Monday-dealers.

text.p: U.S. Midwest direct cash hog prices on Monday were seen mostly steady in light trading, with several major packers scheduling closings in observance of the Easter holiday, livestock dealers said.

Hormel Foods Corp said its plants in Austin, Minn., and Fremont, Neb., will be closed. Farmland Industries said its four hog and pork plants will be closed. ConAgra Inc's Swift and Co unit will close its hog plant in Worthington, Minn.
It will be business as usual at all of IBP Inc's seven pork plants and Excel Corp's three hog plants. Excel Corp is a divsion of Cargill Inc.

Smithfield Foods said its four pork plants in North Carolina and Virginia will be closed on Monday, but two other pork plants operated by its subsidiary, John Morrell and Co in Sioux City, Iowa, and Sioux Falls, S.D., will be open.
Interior Iowa and southern Minnesota top hog prices at the plant on Monday could range $50.00 to $50.50 per cwt.
Illinois top prices for hogs delivered to the plant could range $50.50 to $51.00, and Indiana/Ohio top prices could span $49.00 to $50.00, the livestock dealers said.
